title: Dispatch: Sol full-review repairs batch D, structural lifecycle invariants (attempt 1)
description:
Repair batch D for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8, from the Sol fresh full review bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.6 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.6`; read S3, S4, S12, S14, S19, S20, S21 in full — every failure family listed must be closed). History: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1`, `.8.4`, `.8.5`. The combatant-lifecycle class (S3/S4) has now survived two repair cycles because fixes patched one write path at a time. This batch must close it STRUCTURALLY, not by another per-path guard. Migration 0037 is authorized for S14 only.

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
STRUCTURAL INVARIANT (closes S3's class): add one function in encounterCombatants.ts, e.g. assertCombatantLifecycle(row, record context), that is called on the FINAL state of every combatant write (updateCombatant, death saves, stabilization, suffocation, clamps, head settlement, start_encounter admission/projection, promotion, recovery resolution) and on every campaign-actor lifecycle write, before commit; a violation throws (the transaction rolls back) with a message naming the violated rule. Invariants:
  I1 exhaustion level 6 → status 'dead'.
  I2 a multi-head creature with head_count 0 → status 'dead'.
  I3 status 'dying' or 'stable' → death_rules 'player-character' and hp_current 0.
  I4 death_rules 'player-character' and hp_current 0 → status is 'dying', 'stable', or 'dead' (never alive/unconscious/escaped/inactive at 0 HP).
  I5 recovery_block set → status 'dying' (a dead/alive/stable creature carries no block).
  I6 hp_current <= effectiveHpMax(hp_max, conditions).
  I7 a stable-recovery schedule exists only on status 'stable' (see S14 for the settled form).
  I8 a dead combatant (or actor lifecycle) never leaves 'dead' through any write (no revival operation exists in this PR); monster-rules ordinary revival-by-healing is the ONE allowed exception, and only when neither I1 nor I2 applied (preserve today's monster behaviour).
  Then make every write path produce valid states:
S3 decisions: (1) explicit 'escaped'/'inactive'/'unconscious' statuses are accepted only for a combatant that is alive with hp above 0 under player-character rules (monster rules unchanged apart from I1/I2/I8); (2) opting into player-character rules is refused for a combatant at 0 HP whose status is not 'dead' (incompatible state); (3) non-damage clamps never override 'dead' (a dead creature's HP is clamped but its status stays dead); (4) start_encounter admission of an EXISTING campaign actor: supplied hpCurrent/status may not move the actor out of dead, dying, or stable, may not raise HP while a recovery block is set, and may not admit an I1/I2 creature as anything but dead — such inputs are refused with an error telling the DM to use the lifecycle tools; alive actors still accept supplied HP (clamped by I6).
S4: ensureCampaignActorFromCombatant (and every promotion of a module/anonymous combatant into a durable campaign actor — find all callers, e.g. activeEffects.ts effect creation and combat closure) writes the source combatant's complete combatLifecycle (death rules, counters, block, schedule, head count, pending own-turn facts) through the same reserved engine seam used by actor sync, in the enclosing transaction, transferring schedule ownership so exactly one projection owns it. Preserve unrelated actor state.
S12: rule:suffocating's known limit becomes a trap statement: applying the drop to 0 hit points as damage through adjust_hp or update_combatant does not block healing or stabilization (and for a character starts ordinary dying), so the suffocation drop and later breathing are recorded with set_suffocation. The timing (breath runs out → survival interval from calc suffocation_survival_rounds → drop at the start of the creature's next turn after that interval) and the target contract (characters; combatants under player-character rules are dying, under monster rules dead) move into set_suffocation's own description. Keep participants valid and the source-timing assertions (adapt them to the tool description).
S14: add migration 0037 with a stable_recovery_settled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK IN (0,1) column on character and on encounter_combatant (follow ADR 0015; regenerate the schema snapshot; update migration list expectations). A due recovery at zero effective maximum regains nothing, clears the schedule fields, sets stable_recovery_settled = 1, and the creature stays stable. The clock/recovery integrity check accepts stable + all-null schedule ONLY when settled = 1 and still rejects every partially null or unsettled-null schedule as incomplete. Any later write that leaves 'stable' clears settled. Include settled in the actor combatLifecycle snapshot. Test: settle at max 0, then multiple further advance_time calls succeed for characters and combatants; reducing exhaustion afterwards does not deadlock; a genuinely incomplete schedule is still rejected.
S19: recover_ammunition's entitlement per ammunition identity = floor(total ORIGINAL expended quantity / 2) from the expenditure rows; returned = min(entitlement, pieces still present); destroy the remaining present pieces; report entitlement, returned, destroyed, unavailable. Update the tool description and the rule:weapon-properties statement wording to match ("half the expended ammunition, rounded down, limited to what is still there").
S20: thread ctx.resolveRulesPack through set_surprised (setSurprisedInTransaction and every profile/head/legendary lookup it performs) and adjust_exhaustion's combatant path (and the new clamp), exactly as update_combatant does. Test with the installed add-on fixture (installLateAmbiguityAddon) for a surprised observer and combatant exhaustion; a genuinely unavailable pack still fails with no writes.
S21: in hpLifecycle.ts applyDamage, damage to a character ALREADY at 0 HP (dying or stable) compares the full damage amount (before temporary HP absorption) with effectiveHpMax for instant death, before failure accounting; temporary HP is still consumed. The initial drop from above 0 keeps the overflow rule (rule:instant-death). Matrix test: dying/stable × critical/non-critical × below/equal/above effective max × temp HP absent/partial/full.

TESTS: an invariant test that drives a generated sequence of tool calls (deterministic seed, at least a few hundred random steps over update_combatant / record_death_save / stabilize_character / set_suffocation / adjust_exhaustion / begin_turn / close + start_encounter for a PC-rules goblin, a monster goblin, and a hydra) and asserts I1-I8 after every step, plus actor/projection parity after every reopen — this is the permanent evidence for the class. Plus the specific failure families from the review for S3, S4, S12, S14, S19, S20, S21. Map each finding to its tests in your notes.
acceptance_criteria: All listed findings repaired with the listed tests incl. the generated invariant sequence test; npm run verify:worktree green before commit; completion report mapping findings to tests in bd notes; bead closed by the child.
notes:
Completion report: committed 7a27c514 (fix: enforce combatant lifecycle invariants).

Files changed: packages/core/data/migrations/0037_stable_recovery_settled.sql; packages/core/data/schema.snapshot.sql; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolAdjustExhaustion.ts, toolRecoverAmmunition.ts, toolSetSuffocation.ts, toolSetSurprised.ts; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts; packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts, ammunition.ts, encounterCombatants.ts, exhaustionMutation.ts, hpLifecycle.ts, mutateState.ts; packages/core/test/actionEconomy.test.ts, ammunition.test.ts, encounterCombatants.test.ts, exhaustion.test.ts, hpLifecycle.test.ts, migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts, persistence.test.ts, rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts.

Decisions: implemented the prescribed I1-I8 final-state checks at combatant and actor lifecycle seams; copied complete combatLifecycle state during promotion and transferred stable schedule ownership; refused incompatible status/HP admission and kept dead precedence through clamps; added migration 0037 stable_recovery_settled for zero-maximum stable recovery; aligned suffocation, ammunition recovery, and add-on resolver contracts; instant death at existing 0 HP now compares the full damage event while still consuming temporary HP. Where a later lifecycle mutation leaves a zero-maximum-settled creature stable, it arms a fresh recovery schedule and clears settled so I7 remains valid. No other design deviation.

Finding to test map: S3 — exhaustion.test.ts dead actor admission and seeded 360-step transition/projection invariant sequence; S4 — encounterCombatants.test.ts lifecycle promotion and close/reopen; S12 — rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts known-limit trap plus set_suffocation description; S14 — hpLifecycle.test.ts character zero-maximum settlement and exhaustion.test.ts combatant settlement/re-arm, plus migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts and persistence.test.ts for migration 0037; S19 — ammunition.test.ts original expenditure entitlement capped by present quantity; S20 — actionEconomy.test.ts add-on-bound set_surprised flow and exhaustion.test.ts combatant exhaustion transition coverage; S21 — hpLifecycle.test.ts dying/stable x critical/noncritical x below/equal/above maximum x absent/partial/full temporary HP matrix.

Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed — 320 test files passed, 2 documented skips; 5,695 tests passed, 3 skipped. git diff --check passed. Branch committed and clean.
